title: Uno nunca sabe
setting: Doña Elena has asked you something at the sink that you would rather answer sideways.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: ¿Y usted no piensa volver a su país algún día?
steps.en: And are you not thinking of going back to your country one day?

options.es: Uno nunca sabe, doña. Uno hace planes y después...
options.en: One never knows, doña. You make plans and then...
options.feedback: Uno is the most useful word in the language. It means I and it does not say I, and it leaves the sentence unfinished on purpose.

options.es: No sé, doña. La verdad no sé.
options.en: I do not know, doña. Honestly I do not know.
options.feedback: Honest and exposed. Uno would have said the same thing with a door still open.
Nobody says never about that in this house. Half the family is abroad and the word costs more than you think.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Es que uno se queda pensando en esas cosas.
steps.en: It is that one is left thinking about those things.

options.es: Sí, doña. A uno le da vueltas y no lo dice.
options.en: Yes, doña. It goes round and round and you do not say it.
options.feedback: She used uno and you answered in uno. Both of you are talking about yourselves and neither of you has admitted it, which is exactly the arrangement.
Warm and it drops the cover. She was speaking about herself behind that word and you have just stepped out from behind it.

options.en: Are you thinking about your son, doña?
options.feedback: She was, and she was talking about him in the third person for a reason. Naming him out loud undoes the whole thing.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Y uno se acostumbra, pero no se olvida.
steps.en: And one gets used to it, but one does not forget.

options.en: That is how it is, doña.
options.feedback: Nothing else needed. She has said the hardest thing she is going to say and she said it about nobody in particular.
She has just told you it does not. Telling a woman her own feeling will pass is not a comfort here.

options.es: Uno aprende a vivir con eso.
options.en: One learns to live with it.
options.feedback: Correct word, and you have just paraphrased her back at her. Silence would have carried more.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Bueno. ¿Me ayuda con esa cebolla, mijo?
steps.en: Well. Will you give me a hand with that onion, son?

options.en: I will give you a hand, doña.
options.feedback: She has closed it with the onion and you take the onion. Nobody in this kitchen is going to say another word about it.
Fine. Say the thing you are doing and the subject is properly buried.

options.es: ¿Y no quiere seguir hablando de eso?
options.en: And do you not want to keep talking about that?
options.feedback: No. The onion is the answer, and asking her to reopen it makes her say out loud that she does not want to.
